correctness.rationale: The explicit Cayley and rook adjacency rules satisfy all (16,6,2,2) strongly regular constraints by exhaustive loops; all 2^16 vertex masks are exhaustively classified into 200/208 nonempty faces. Two algorithmic methods reproduce independence polynomials. 88/96 exact codimension-one matching pairs leave only 1 critical zero-cell and 23/15 critical two-cells. Complete Hasse-orientation DAG topological sorts process all 200/208 cells and all 496/528 incidence arrows. The finite discrete Morse theorem gives the wedges and integral homology without inferring homotopy merely from experimental Betti numbers. Both standalone embedded programs were run successfully.

value.rationale: The natural smallest pair of nonisomorphic strongly regular graphs with identical parameters and spectra is a motivated comparison. Their independence complexes also agree in face counts through dimension two, yet their reduced integral degree-two homology differs by rank eight. The novel Shrikhande homotopy type is a complete, reproducible, small topological invariant, mathematically stronger than face-count or eigenvalue discrimination; its topological comparison does not claim these graphs were previously indistinguishable.
